description: 2 tactical challenges for Black in the Blackburne Shilling Gambit. Lure White with 3...Nd4!? and punish the greedy 4.Nxe5??.

drills.briefExplanation: 3...Nd4 4.Nxe5?? Qg5! 5.Bxf7+ Ke7 6.O-O Qxe5 — the queen forks g2 and e5, and Black wins a piece.
drills.description: Black to play. White develops 3.Bc4 — offer the Shilling Gambit with 3...Nd4!.
drills.explanation: Blackburne's trap: 3...Nd4 looks like it hangs the e-pawn, and 4.Nxe5?? grabs it — falling into 4...Qg5!, attacking the knight and threatening mate on g2. After 5.Bxf7+ Ke7 6.O-O Black simply plays 6...Qxe5, emerging a piece up: the 'free' pawn cost White a knight. Never trust a pawn that looks too free.
drills.name: The Shilling Trap

drills.briefExplanation: 4.c3 Nxf3+ 5.Qxf3 Qf6 — trade knights with check, then hit the queen and the b2 pawn.
drills.description: Black to play. White avoids 4.Nxe5 with 4.c3 — find the other Shilling idea.
drills.explanation: 4.c3 looks solid, but the Shilling has a second sting: 4...Nxf3+! 5.Qxf3 Qf6 attacks the queen and eyes b2. White's center is loosened (the c-pawn advanced, the d-pawn is backward) and Black's queen is aggressively placed — full compensation for the slightly awkward knight trade, with ...Bc5 and ...d6 to follow.
drills.name: The c3 Punishment

name: Blackburne Shilling Gambit — Black Tactics
